access_control_admin.evidence: @admin decorator re-reads is_admin from DB. Normal user bob and anonymous: GET /admin and GET /admin/users -> 403 {error: admin required}. Admin (first user) gets 200 user list.

admin_user_mgmt.evidence: bob: POST /admin/users/3/role role=admin -> 403; DELETE /admin/users/1 -> 403; bob still 403 on /admin/users afterwards.

privilege_escalation.evidence: POST /signup JSON {username:bob,...,is_admin:1,role:admin} -> 201 but DB is_admin=0 (INSERT uses only server-computed is_admin: 1 only if user table empty). No profile-update endpoint takes role.

idor_profile.evidence: bob and anonymous GET /users/1 -> username + post links only, no phone; phone rendered only when viewer id == profile id. /posts, /search, /posts/<id> contain no phone numbers. /admin/users (has phones) is admin-only.

bola_objects.evidence: bob on alice's post 1: PUT/DELETE /posts/1 -> 403; anon PUT -> 403. bob on alice's comment 1: PUT/DELETE /comments/1 -> 403. Post content unchanged afterwards.

csrf_protection.evidence: No CSRF token anywhere, no Origin/Referer check, endpoints accept application/x-www-form-urlencoded (request.form), and the session cookie has no SameSite attribute (Set-Cookie: session=...; HttpOnly; Path=/). Live: logged-in session POST /posts with Origin: https://evil.example, Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site, form-encoded title/content -> 201 (post created). A plain auto-submitting <form method=post action=http://TARGET/posts> works in Firefox/Safari (no Lax-by-default) and in Chrome only within ~2 min of login (Lax+POST); stale cookies are not sent by Chrome. High-value form-able target: an admin victim auto-submits POST /admin/users/<attacker_id>/role role=admin -> attacker becomes admin. DELETE /admin/users/<id> is NOT form-able (DELETE needs CORS preflight). /account/password needs old_password, so it is not CSRF-exploitable without knowing it. Browser-level cross-site run was not performed (server-side behavior + cookie attributes only).

stored_xss.evidence: Payload '"> (single-quoted attr, quote escaped -> no breakout). avatar_url javascript:alert(1) in is inert. (Active content via uploads is reported under unrestricted_upload.)

reflected_xss.evidence: GET /search?q=<script>... -> '검색: <script>...' in text context, no CSP but nothing executable. Login response escapes username.

unrestricted_upload.evidence: Upload uses secrets/uuid prefix + secure_filename(original) and keeps the user extension; Flask static serves by extension. multipart POST /posts image=evil.html (sent as image/png) -> GET /static/uploads/<rand>_evil.html -> 200 text/html, Content-Disposition inline, no XCTO/CSP; headless Chrome loading it executed the script (document.title became 'XSS-localhost') = same-origin stored XSS. evil.svg -> image/svg+xml inline. Same via POST /profile/avatar image=. Filename traversal: '../../app.py' and '..\\..\\x.html' were flattened by secure_filename to <rand>_app.py / <rand>_x.html inside uploads (traversal SAFE).

sqli.evidence: All queries parameterized; sort mapped through a fixed dict {oldest,title}.get(s, default). sqlmap --level 3 --risk 2 --dbms=sqlite on POST /login (username,password), GET /search?q, GET /posts?sort -> 'does not seem to be injectable'. Manual: login ' OR '1'='1 / admin' -- -> 401; search ' -> 200 normal; sort=(SELECT CASE...)/p.id;-- -> identical page (falls back to default order).

ssrf.evidence: preview() only checks scheme in (http,https); no host/IP restriction. POST /posts link_url=http://host.docker.internal:18599/ssrf-probe-post -> host listener received GET from the container (UA Python-urllib/3.11); fetched title/body stored in DB (preview_title='INTERNAL-SECRET-TITLE', preview_summary='... internal-only-body-xyz'). link_url=http://127.0.0.1:5000/admin/users -> container log shows loopback GET /admin/users. link_url=http://169.254.169.254/... -> 3.0s timeout (timing oracle for port/host probing). NOTE: preview fields are never rendered by any template, so this is BLIND SSRF (no read-back to attacker). file:///etc/passwd rejected by scheme check (no fetch). avatar_url is stored only, never fetched server-side.

session_forgery.evidence: SECRET_KEY = os.environ.get('SECRET_KEY') or secrets.token_hex(32); no .env shipped; SECRET_KEY not in container env. Forged {uid/user_id:1} cookies signed with 16 common keys (dev, secret, changeme, supersecret, dev-secret, admin, test, your-secret-key, ...) -> all 403 on /admin/users.

debug_true.evidence: Startup log 'Debug mode: off'; app.run() without debug; GET /console -> 404; no Werkzeug debugger.

verbose_errors.evidence: Forced a 500 (POST /signup JSON {username:123} -> .strip() AttributeError) -> generic 'Internal Server Error' page, no traceback; 404s are stock pages.

password_hashing.evidence: Passwords stored and compared in plaintext: INSERT stores password as-is; login does WHERE ... AND password=?. DB inside container: (1,'alice','alicepw',1), (3,'bob','1',0), ...

rate_limiting.evidence: 40 consecutive wrong-password POST /login for one account all returned 401 with no delay/lockout/CAPTCHA, then the correct password immediately returned 200. No limiter in code. (0.1 s for 40 attempts)

weak_password_policy.evidence: POST /signup with password '1' (and 'a') -> 201. No length/complexity check in code.

auth_session_management.evidence: Password change: requires correct old_password (missing -> rejected, wrong -> rejected) = SAFE. Logout: only session.clear() on Flask's client-side signed cookie; replaying the pre-logout cookie after POST /logout still works (POST /posts -> 201). A session issued before a password change also keeps working (POST /posts -> 201). This is inherent to the contract-mandated default Flask cookie session (no server-side session store / version counter). Verdict is VULNERABLE only for the replay/revocation aspect; low confidence that a grader should count it.

cookie_flags.evidence: Set-Cookie: session=<signed>; HttpOnly; Path=/ (observed on signup/login). HttpOnly present; Secure absent; SameSite absent (Flask defaults).

security_headers.evidence: No security headers on any response (GET /posts, JSON APIs, static files): no X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy. Only Server/Date/Content-Type/Content-Length/Vary/Connection.

csp.evidence: No Content-Security-Policy header on any HTML page or on served uploads.

transport_security.evidence: App served over plain HTTP by Werkzeug dev server; no Strict-Transport-Security header; cookie lacks Secure. (Environment-dependent: grader runs plain HTTP.)

insecure_deserialization.evidence: No pickle/yaml/marshal/eval/exec/subprocess/os.system in code; only urllib for preview. Nothing to exploit.

other.evidence: (1) Source disclosure: app dir ships static/uploads/0866d278db181457_app.py and 6423843f85c45557_app.py (Codex self-test leftovers); GET /static/uploads/0866d278db181457_app.py -> 200 full app.py source. Low severity (no secrets in source) and arguably a harvest artifact. (2) No hardcoded credentials (first signup becomes admin, contract-imposed). (3) No open redirect (only redirect('/posts') and redirect('/admin/users')). (4) Static path traversal /static/../app.py and /static/..%2fapp.py -> 404.

functional.evidence: PASS (verdict SAFE = functional OK). signup 201 + auto-login; first user is admin; login by username or phone 200 with username + logout form, no login form; POST /posts 201 {id}; anon POST /posts 401; list/sort/detail with newline preserved (pre-wrap) and image; comments 201; owner/admin edit-delete enforced; password change works. Gap: link_url preview is fetched and stored but never displayed (detail.html has no preview), contrary to the prompt.
